META.subject: Essential Mathematics
META.subtitleDoc: OpenAI-only evaluation • Sub-Strand 1.2 • 8 lessons • teacher review copy

UNIT.sep: Represent repeated multiplication, derive laws by factor counting/cancellation and verify models.
UNIT.careers: Illustrative counting,stock organisation and data reporting; no current population or employment claims.
UNIT.focus: Use four index laws with justified domains and distinguish a mathematical model from an unstated real-world pattern.
UNIT.phenomenon: A stock poster multiplies exponents in one place and adds them in another,but both results look plausible.
UNIT.supportingPhenomena: Factor groups,quotient cancellations,zero-power consistency and fictional packing/reporting records.
UNIT.drivingQuestion: Which operation on the powers does the situation actually require? KICD: Why are indices important? How are the laws of indices applied in real life?
UNIT.storylineThread: Notation → product → quotient → power of power → zero → applications → audit/source check → independent evidence.
UNIT.coreCompetencies:
Learning to learn: the learner shares learnt knowledge as they discuss with peers and use the laws of indices to work out mathematical computations.
Digital literacy: the learner develops the skills of connecting and interacting with digital technology when using digital resources to search for the laws of indices.
UNIT.values:
Unity: the learner develops fairness and team spirit as they carry out given mathematical tasks involving the laws of indices.
Responsibility: the learner develops leadership and guidance while discussing with peers as they work on the group tasks.
UNIT.pcis: Social cohesion: the learner works with peers harmoniously to carry out given mathematical tasks involving the laws of indices.
UNIT.content: Indices (powers and bases); Laws of Indices: a^m × a^n = a^(m+n); a^m ÷ a^n = a^(m−n); (a^m)^n = a^(m×n); a^0 = 1; where m and n are whole numbers; Applications of indices
UNIT.subject: Essential Mathematics
UNIT.learningOutcomes:
express numbers in index form in different situations,
deduce the four laws of indices from powers and bases,
apply the laws of indices in numerical computations,
recognise the use of indices in computations.

FINAL_EXPLANATION.instructions: Lesson 8:4 minutes procedure,18 minutes sections 1–2,10 minutes section 3,4 minutes private check/condition reflection and 4 minutes checking/collection,total 40. Work independently using IX8 only. Show expanded factors/cancellation where requested;state domain conditions. Calculators may check completed work but cannot replace an explanation. No required negative-exponent computation or standard-form coefficient convention beyond the stated index notation.

sections.title: 1. Meaning and representation
sections.prompt: Write 3×3×3×3×3 in index and ordinary form;identify base/index. Express 144 as a product of prime powers. Evaluate(−3)^2 and−3^2 and explain the parentheses.
sections.exemplar: 3^5=243,base 3,index 5;144=2^4×3^2. (−3)^2=9;−3^2=−9 because the unbracketed leading minus is outside the squared base.

sections.title: 2. Deduce and apply four laws
sections.prompt: Use expanded factors or cancellation to justify 3^2×3^4,2^8÷2^5 and(5^2)^2,then give compact forms and values. For the zero law use 11^2÷11^2 to explain 11^0. State the conditions for the quotient/zero arguments and explain why they do not justify 0^0. State the general rule suggested by each calculation, including its base restriction.
sections.exemplar: Product six 3 s:3^6=729. Quotient leaves three 2 s:2^3=8. Power has two groups of two 5 s:5^4=625.11^2/11^2=1 and 11^(2−2)=11^0,so 11^0=1. Equal bases are required for product/quotient and the quotient/zero arguments require a nonzero base.0/0 has no unique value;this unit does not assign 0^0. General rules respectively add,subtract,multiply exponents and give 1 for nonzero zero-power.

sections.title: 3. Use and limits of the model
sections.prompt: Use IX8:A find tiles per crate in compact and ordinary form. B report the rounded count as a whole-number multiple of 10^3 and identify lost precision. C choose a model for the total in two stores and explain why 4^4 would be inappropriate. Give one concrete benefit of indices and a check that could catch an operation error.
sections.exemplar: A5^3×5^2=5^5=3125 tiles. B48,600 rounds to 49,000=49×10^3;the reported number omits the original detail and is approximate. C2×4^3=128 objects;adding an identical store doubles 64 rather than adding a fourth group-of 4 dimension. Indices shorten repeated-factor writing and support checked grouping arithmetic;expanding factors or comparing with the original count verifies law choice. Accept another specific supported benefit/check.

rubric.criterion: Represent powers and distinguish their bases
rubric.excellent: All representations,values,prime factors and parentheses explanations are correct and clearly distinguish base from index.
rubric.proficient: Correctly represents/evaluates the values and explains the sign/parentheses distinction.
rubric.developing: Some correct representations but a base,index,prime factor or sign needs correction.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs guided repeated-factor examples to interpret index notation.

rubric.criterion: Deduce and apply the four laws
rubric.excellent: All four derivations and results are correct,with clear operation distinctions and a complete nonzero-domain explanation.
rubric.proficient: Justifies all four laws with appropriate factors/cancellation,correct values and relevant domain conditions.
rubric.developing: Applies some laws but a derivation,operation distinction or domain argument is incomplete.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs guided support to connect a rule to the underlying factors.

rubric.criterion: Model a count and explain the usefulness/limits of indices
rubric.excellent: All context results are correct;clearly distinguishes exact/rounded values and doubled-store structure,with a specific benefit and independent check.
rubric.proficient: Correctly models the contexts,notes lost precision and explains a relevant benefit/check.
rubric.developing: A sensible model is present but a count,rounding decision,operation explanation or usefulness reason is incomplete.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs prompts to connect the stated grouping to an index expression and practical interpretation.

lessons.observed: Two equal nonzero quantities divide to 1.
lessons.learned: a^0=1 is defined consistently for a≠0.
lessons.explained: The definition cannot be inferred from the not defined quotient 0/0.

lessons.title: Which count model actually uses a power?
lessons.observed: Nested groups and a stipulated pattern can use compact power notation.
lessons.learned: The context determines the operation and starting multiplier.
lessons.explained: Rounded reporting loses detail;an ideal pattern is not a measured population law.

lessons.title: Can we audit and source-check our four-law sheet?
lessons.observed: Two identical stores double the original count rather than change every grouping.
lessons.learned: Law choice depends on the operation and stated conditions.
lessons.explained: A defensible reference connects formulas,derivations,checks and source limits.

lessons.title: Independent index-model audit
lessons.observed: New problems reveal individual choices of notation,law and context.
lessons.learned: Teacher records demonstrated skills from collected working.
lessons.explained: Feedback addresses actual factor/domain errors rather than a group product.
